signs.name: Solid perception
signs.definition: The first sign of full composition: the film organises every image around one central, privileged body. The camera oscillates between seeing as that character (point of view) and seeing that character, producing a cohesive perceiving-and-perceived subject, a 'solid I'.
signs.deamer_quote: “all other filmic images circulate around this body” (p. 78)
deleuze_examples: Lady in the Lake (Robert Montgomery, 1947) – whole film as the detective's point-of-view shot (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Deamer (after Mitry, C1: 72) describes the 'being-with' as shot–reverse-shot couplings between a character's POV and shots looking at that character; no film named

section3.film: The Diving Bell and the Butterfly (Julian Schnabel, 2007)
scenes: Opening awakening shot from Jean-Do's eyes: blurred, flickering image framed by eyelids, blinks acting as jump-cuts and fades to black.
Bed-bound fixed POV restricted to wall and ceiling; doctors and nurses lean in too close or hover half out of frame.
His failing eye is sewn shut from the inside: needle and thread closing the frame itself.
Later he is placed in frame: wrapped in blankets on the hospital balcony, then with his children on a windswept beach, still the centre of every image.

signs.operation: Bind the camera to one perceiver's eyes, then turn it round to look at that body, until every image in the film orbits a single subject.
signs.shot_criteria: Either a clear point-of-view shot (framing that stands in for a person's eyes: looking down at own hands, through a vehicle windscreen, up from a bed or through binoculars/keyhole), or a single figure held dead-centre with the world arranged around them.
signs.gloss: all images revolve around a central and privileged image
signs.question: Whose world is this?

diff.name: Solid perception
diff.difference: One body owns the frame: either we see through its eyes (POV, eyelid/mask/windscreen framing) or we see it held at the hub with everything else arranged around it — and the image would lose its organising centre if that body were removed.
diff.axis: perceptual centre: one privileged body ([SOLID — here]) → centres that form and dissolve (Liquid) → no centre (Gaseous)

confusions.name: Liquid perception
confusions.flip: It is Liquid instead if the camera keeps moving and the centre visibly hands off — the figure exits or is overtaken and the frame re-centres on another person, place or event within the shot or cut.
confusions.why_not: In Solid the camera returns to the same body; the privilege is stable, not momentary.

confusions.name: Icon
confusions.flip: It is Icon instead if the frame is a close-up in which the face itself is the whole image — expression cut off from space and motor outlet — rather than a person positioned as the axis of a surrounding world.
confusions.why_not: Solid perception is about where perception is anchored (a body among sets, objects, others), not about a face expressing an intensity; a typical Solid shot shows the world as seen by or arranged around the subject.

confusions.name: Opsign (pure optical situation)
confusions.flip: It is an opsign instead if the POV-holder is a seer who cannot act on what they see — the look no longer extends into movement or response and the scene simply overwhelms or stalls the viewer.
confusions.why_not: Solid perception is the first sign of a sensory-motor world: the subject perceives in order to feel and act; the POV is linked to reverse shots and to movement.

diff.counterfeit: A generic handheld 'found-footage' camera that happens to belong to a character but keeps swinging to whatever is loudest looks like POV yet builds no privileged perceiver — it is closer to liquid or gaseous perception.

confidence.high: An unmistakable subjective framing (eyelid blur, binocular mask, own hands/feet in frame) or a figure dead-centre with the whole mise-en-scène converging on them, and ideally a POV/reverse-shot pair.
confidence.medium: A plain centred medium shot of one figure or a POV-like angle without masking — plausibly Solid, but centring alone is ordinary framing grammar.
confidence.low: Any single frame where it is unknown whether the film keeps returning to that body; Deamer's criterion is that the centre is in every shot of the film, which one shot cannot prove.

diff.deamer_anchor: "all other filmic images circulate around this body" (p. 78)

signs.name: Liquid perception
signs.definition: The secondary sign of composition: a mobile camera and flowing montage pass from environment to environment and character to character, so centres form only for a moment before the film flows on to the next.
signs.deamer_quote: “Liquid perception puts the camera into motion, a flowing movement of continuous reframing.” (p. 79)
deleuze_examples: L'Atalante (Jean Vigo, 1934) – the river barge and water imagery of the French prewar school (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
L'Homme du large (Marcel L'Herbier, 1920) – sea and liquid movement (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Finis Terrae (Jean Epstein, 1929) – islands, tides, rolling sea (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Deamer names the technique rather than a film: tracking shots, crane shots and Steadicams joining different spaces

scenes: Handheld long take: Lauren deflates Rose's tyre in a mansion driveway and the camera, without a cut, tilts to become Rose's gaze when she spots the flat.
The screen split into four simultaneous single-take quadrants (therapy session, lovers, a security monitor, a masseur crossing a busy boulevard) the eye flows between.
The masseur walks into an office block in one quadrant and at the same moment into the foyer seen in another.
Periodic small earthquakes shake every quadrant at once: solid ground turning liquid.

signs.operation: Keep the camera moving and never cut: follow one person until someone else crosses the frame, then let them carry the shot onward.
signs.shot_criteria: A visibly moving camera (tracking, crane, dolly, handheld follow) that passes between people or spaces within the shot, or a flowing water/boat-mounted movement where no single figure holds the centre.
signs.gloss: the flow from character/event to character/event
signs.question: Does perception migrate?

diff.name: Liquid perception
diff.difference: The centre moves: in a continuous reframing the shot passes from one character or environment to another, each central only until the next captures the screen.
diff.axis: perceptual centre: one privileged body (Solid) → centres that form and dissolve ([LIQUID — here]) → no centre (Gaseous)

confusions.name: Solid perception
confusions.flip: It is Solid instead if, however much the camera travels, it stays locked to one protagonist (a follow-shot behind one walker).
confusions.why_not: A typical Liquid shot relinquishes its figure; the tracking movement is loyal to the flow, not to a person.

confusions.name: Gaseous perception
confusions.flip: It is Gaseous instead if no centre ever forms — time-lapse, superimposition, micro-shooting or manipulated stock make human figures one image among clouds, traffic and matter.
confusions.why_not: In Liquid perception centres do coalesce (a character, an event), just only for a moment; the image remains human-scaled and continuous in time.

confusions.name: Dividual
confusions.flip: It is Dividual instead if the travelling camera over many people is expressing one shared affect of the mass — panic, joy, grief — rather than passing attention from centre to centre.
confusions.why_not: Liquid perception concerns the organisation of perception (the flow of centres), not the expression of a collective feeling; its crowds can be affectively neutral.

diff.counterfeit: A showy Steadicam 'oner' that follows one hero through a nightclub is often called fluid but is Solid perception in motion — the centre never passes on.

confidence.high: A single long mobile take in which the camera visibly abandons one figure to pick up another (and ideally another), or a split/multi-frame image of parallel centres (Timecode).
confidence.medium: A crane or tracking shot through a populated space where it is unclear whether anyone is privileged; or smooth continuity cutting between ensemble members.
confidence.low: A still frame or a static ensemble shot — the sign is a movement of passage and cannot be read from a frozen image.

diff.deamer_anchor: centres "central only for a moment, becoming subordinate" (p. 79)

signs.name: Gaseous perception
signs.definition: The genetic sign of perception: an acentred, non-human perception in which all images interact without hierarchy, achieved through slow and fast motion, superimposition, fragmentation, micro-shooting and manipulated film; any human figure is just one image among landscapes, animals and matter.
signs.deamer_quote: “all images interacting with one another without hierarchy” (p. 79)
deleuze_examples: Man with a Movie Camera (Dziga Vertov, 1929) – the 'cine-eye': superimposition, split screens, speed changes (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
La Région Centrale (Michael Snow, 1971) – machine-driven camera sweeping an empty landscape (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
American experimental cinema (Stan Brakhage) – hand-worked, grainy, molecular images (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)

scenes: Slow zoom into a 3D rendering of Bruegel's Little Tower of Babel, then a black digital grid of white contour lines erupting into a similar spiral structure.
A raging sea heavily digitised; clouds racing in fast motion mirrored in a still river.
Close-up of a baby's face; the camera pulls back and up to reveal many identical babies duplicated across a white clinical surface.
Crowds in slow motion and negative; bodies seen through X-ray, brain scan and thermal imaging.

signs.operation: Take the human out of the centre: speed up, slow down, multiply and superimpose images until the frame perceives like matter rather than a person.
signs.shot_criteria: A visibly non-human or manipulated image: time-lapse, extreme slow motion, superimposition/multiple exposure, negative, microscopy, X-ray or thermal view, or a kaleidoscopic/duplicated pattern where no subject dominates.
signs.gloss: all images resonate with one another as an acentred system
signs.question: Can the world perceive without a human center?

diff.name: Gaseous perception
diff.difference: Nothing is privileged: through slow/fast motion, superimposition, fragmentation or micro-shooting the image treats a human figure as one image like any other among landscapes, matter and machines.
diff.axis: perceptual centre: one privileged body (Solid) → centres that form and dissolve (Liquid) → no centre ([GASEOUS — here])

confusions.name: Liquid perception
confusions.flip: It is Liquid instead if, despite the flow, the image settles for a moment on a character or event we are invited to follow.
confusions.why_not: Gaseous perception never lets a centre stabilise; its figures are not followed, they are processed.

confusions.name: Any-space-whatever
confusions.flip: It is Any-space-whatever instead if the acentred space is held as an affective quality — fog, a coloured void, a ruin that expresses a mood — rather than as interacting matter-images in variation.
confusions.why_not: Gaseous perception is defined by technical variation and interaction of images (speeds, superimposition); the any-space-whatever by the affect of an emptied or disconnected space, often static.

confusions.name: Opsign (pure optical situation)
confusions.flip: It is an opsign instead if the acentred image is lived by a seer as a stalled situation — a character stranded before an image they can neither extend into action nor escape.
confusions.why_not: Deamer places Gaseous inside the movement-image: its variation still forms an assemblage of enunciation and a conception of the whole, not a crisis of a perceiving character.

diff.counterfeit: An ordinary time-lapse establishing shot of a city skyline used to say 'next morning, New York' looks gaseous but functions as a Milieu establishing shot in a centred narrative.

confidence.high: Visible machinic manipulation (time-lapse, multiple exposure, extreme speed changes, microscopic or grain-level imagery) in which humans appear at the same scale and weight as clouds, cells or cars.
confidence.medium: Abstract or experimental imagery without clear human reference — could be Gaseous, Any-space-whatever or simply texture.
confidence.low: A single slow-motion shot of a character inside a narrative: technique alone does not dissolve the centre.

diff.deamer_anchor: "any human image an image like any other" (p. 80)

signs.name: Icon
signs.definition: The first sign of the affection-image: the close-up of the face, which expresses unfilmable inner intensities either as an immobile quality (a face fixed in wonder on an object) or as a mobile power (features passing from one state to the next toward action).
signs.deamer_quote: “The icon is a close-up of the face” (p. 82)
deleuze_examples: The Passion of Joan of Arc (Carl Th. Dreyer, 1928) – Joan's tear-streaked face in unbroken close-ups (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Broken Blossoms (D.W. Griffith, 1919) – Lillian Gish's face in close-up (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
The Blue Angel / Shanghai Express (Josef von Sternberg) – Dietrich's lit face as reflecting surface (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Persona (Ingmar Bergman, 1966) – merged faces and the face's effacement (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)

scenes: Malli in extreme close-up: large luminous eyes, lips, skin, held almost silent except for breathing and nature sounds.
Malli as hidden observer, lost in recollection, the camera staying on her eyes and mouth for a 'little eternity'.
Treating medium and full shots as close-ups: the whole film organised by the face rather than the plot of the assassination.
The ending: her face as she stands at the rally with the bomb beneath her sari, the choice never shown.

signs.operation: Move in until the face fills the frame and hold it past the point of information, so expression becomes the event.
signs.shot_criteria: A close-up or extreme close-up in which a single face (or eyes/mouth) fills most of the frame and carries visible emotion or intense attention.
signs.gloss: the face expressing unfilmable internal intensities
signs.question: Where does intensity become a face?

diff.name: Icon
diff.difference: The face is not a feature of a person in a space but the whole image: a close-up in which expression (fixed wonder or traversing micro-movements) holds an intensity that has not yet become action.
diff.axis: affect carrier: a face ([ICON — here]) → a mass / collective (Dividual) → a space (Any-space-whatever)

confusions.name: Dividual
confusions.flip: It is Dividual instead if the face is one of a series of faces or bodies that together express one collective emotion, the individual standing in for the mass.
confusions.why_not: The Icon's intensity is concentrated in a single face; it does not depend on multiplicity.

confusions.name: Symptom
confusions.flip: It is Symptom instead if the facial intensity has already tipped into a primordial act — gnawing, biting, lunging, grabbing — the face as the site of an impulse too strong for the character.
confusions.why_not: The Icon suspends between perception and action (quality or power not yet actualised); the Symptom is the short-circuit where the impulse acts.

confusions.name: Body of attitude
confusions.flip: It is Body of attitude instead if the close attention falls on the body's postures, fatigue and waiting over duration — a body that carries time — rather than on a face expressing a feeling.
confusions.why_not: The Icon remains in the sensory-motor schema as affect between perception and action; body of attitude belongs to the time-image, where the body is not a centre of action at all.

diff.counterfeit: A close-up of a character speaking dialogue in a shot/reverse-shot exchange is framed like an Icon but functions as action-image coverage: the face transmits information, not an intensity cut from its situation.

confidence.high: A tight close-up where the face fills the frame, background blurred or blank, and either immobile rapt expression or visible passage of micro-expressions; no speech carrying plot.
confidence.medium: A medium close-up with some setting visible, or an expressive face that is also clearly reacting to a legible event.
confidence.low: A face in a wide or medium shot, or a talking head; the close-up is Deamer's fundamental condition.

diff.deamer_anchor: "The icon is a close-up of the face" (p. 82)

signs.name: Dividual
signs.definition: The secondary sign of the affection-image: affect expressed by a mass – crowd, pack, multitude – where individuals are de-individualised and the group is individualised, uniting a collective reflection with each person's emotion.
signs.deamer_quote: “The camera traverses a series of faces, captures bodies in a gathering” (p. 84)
deleuze_examples: Battleship Potemkin (Sergei Eisenstein, 1925) – Odessa steps crowd and mourners by Vakulinchuk's body (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
The Passion of Joan of Arc (Dreyer, 1928) – the judges as a gallery of faces forming one tribunal (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Strike (Eisenstein, 1925) – the massed strikers (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)

section3.film: Despicable Me / Despicable Me 2 / Minions (Coffin, Renaud, Balda, 2010–2015)
scenes: 'Minions assemble!': hundreds of identical yellow minions swarm out of labs, docks and gantries of Gru's underground base.
The horde pours into the tiered arena to hear the plan – a mass of near-identical bodies each with a small difference (one eye, two eyes, hair).
Minions working forklifts, riding winches, snacking at water coolers, doing gym class: a workforce as a single affective organism.
Minions follows three individuations (Stuart, Kevin, Bob) who carry the whole tribe's desire to find a master.

signs.operation: Pan across a gathering until the faces merge into one feeling, then find the one face that carries the whole crowd.
signs.shot_criteria: A crowd, pack, flock or massed group sharing one visible reaction or motion (cheering, fleeing, marching, swarming), ideally with individual faces still legible within the mass.
signs.gloss: the conjunction of collective and individual affects
signs.question: Is the feeling mine, ours, or both?

diff.name: Dividual
diff.difference: The feeling belongs to the gathering: the crowd, pack or series of faces is individualised as one affect while each person in it is de-individualised.
diff.axis: affect carrier: a face (Icon) → a mass / collective ([DIVIDUAL — here]) → a space (Any-space-whatever)

confusions.name: Icon
confusions.flip: It is Icon instead if the camera isolates one face in close-up and the emotion reads as that person's own, not the crowd's reflected in them.
confusions.why_not: The Dividual needs the conjunction of collective and individual; a single face alone cannot carry it unless it is shown to embody a population.

confusions.name: Milieu
confusions.flip: It is Milieu instead if the mass is shown as the social situation — workers at a factory gate in an extreme wide shot establishing place, class and history — rather than as an affect.
confusions.why_not: In the Dividual the crowd expresses feeling (panic, ecstasy, grief); in the Milieu it exemplifies a determined geo-historical situation.

confusions.name: Liquid perception
confusions.flip: It is Liquid instead if the camera moving through the crowd is passing attention from one centre to the next without a shared emotional charge.
confusions.why_not: A typical Dividual shot is unified by one affect traversing all bodies; the movement serves the affect, not the circulation of centres.

diff.counterfeit: An extras-filled background behind a protagonist looks collective but is only set dressing — the crowd has no affect of its own and the shot is Solid perception or an Icon.

confidence.high: Many bodies or a rapid series of faces all gripped by the same visible emotion (fleeing, cheering, mourning), with no single protagonist privileged.
confidence.medium: A crowd shot whose emotional unity is ambiguous, or a group of a few characters sharing a reaction.
confidence.low: A crowd that is merely present, or a single figure claimed to 'stand for' the people without visual evidence.

diff.deamer_anchor: "the individualisation of a mass" (p. 84)

signs.name: Any-space-whatever
signs.definition: The genetic sign of the affection-image: an empty, disconnected or amorphous space – fog, rain, shadow, ruin, heat haze, a pure coloured or blank background – that expresses affect directly, without a face, prior to or after the human.
signs.deamer_quote: “Any-space-whatevers utilise an empty or disconnected mise-en-scène” (p. 84)
deleuze_examples: Pickpocket (Robert Bresson, 1959) – the fragmented spaces of the Gare de Lyon (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Rain (Joris Ivens, 1929) – Amsterdam dissolved into rain and reflections (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
German Expressionism (e.g. Nosferatu, Murnau 1922) – shadow and light as intensive space (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Deamer (quoting C2: xi): 'disused warehouses, waste ground, cities in the course of demolition'

section3.film: Le quattro volte / Four Times (Michelangelo Frammartino, 2010)
scenes: A single 180-degree panning long take of a country lane: a dog patters, a truck of costumed centurions arrives, a procession forms and leaves.
The old goatherd Fuda shot small within ragged mountains and open fields, never overwhelming the landscape.
A lone tree filmed through summer, autumn, winter and spring before it is cut down.
The smoking charcoal mound: dead wood stacked and burning into inorganic carbon, filmed as pure space and duration.

signs.operation: Empty the frame of people and hold on the space – fog, rain, ruin, glare – until the place itself becomes the feeling.
signs.shot_criteria: A shot with no human focus (or a tiny, overwhelmed figure) where the space itself dominates: fog, rain, heat haze, lens flare, deep shadow, ruin, empty interior or blank backdrop.
signs.gloss: the expression of non-human affects
signs.question: Has place stopped functioning as ordinary geography?

diff.name: Any-space-whatever
diff.difference: Affect with no face: an emptied, disconnected or amorphous space (fog, rain, shadow, coloured void, ruin, haze) that expresses a quality itself rather than locating an action.
diff.axis: affect carrier: a face (Icon) → a mass / collective (Dividual) → a space ([ANY-SPACE-WHATEVER — here])

confusions.name: Originary world
confusions.flip: It is Originary world instead if the space is a determinate archetypal place — this desert, this forest, the house — charged with primal forces that are about to seize bodies, under a time of decay.
confusions.why_not: Deleuze/Deamer: the originary world may resemble an any-space-whatever but appears only in the depths of a determined milieu; the any-space-whatever is indeterminate affect, not a lair of drives.

confusions.name: Opsign (pure optical situation)
confusions.flip: It is an opsign instead if the space is freed from any sensory-motor linkage — no character will act on it, nothing it expresses feeds a next action — and is simply seen, with the seer stranded before it.
confusions.why_not: Within the movement-image the any-space-whatever is the intensive ground of characters traversing it from perception to action; Deamer says it becomes an opsign only when set free from those linkages.

confusions.name: Dividual
confusions.flip: It is Dividual instead if bodies gather in the space and the affect reads as theirs collectively rather than as the space's.
confusions.why_not: The any-space-whatever is the ground out of which the dividual assembles; in its pure form the human is absent or overwhelmed.

diff.counterfeit: A beautiful empty landscape used as a transition or location card ('Two weeks later — Montana') looks like an any-space-whatever but is a determinate place establishing a Milieu.

confidence.high: No human figure (or a figure dwarfed and overwhelmed), space made indeterminate by fog, darkness, flat colour, flare or haze, held long enough to read as a quality.
confidence.medium: A recognisable place emptied of action — could equally be Milieu (if informative), Originary world (if menacing) or opsign (if a seer is stranded).
confidence.low: Any empty frame without context: the difference from opsign is the relation to surrounding action, which one shot cannot show.

diff.deamer_anchor: "an empty or disconnected mise-en-scène" (p. 84)

signs.name: Symptom
signs.definition: The first sign of the impulse-image: a character overwhelmed by a primal impulse too strong for them (hunger, sex, greed, cruelty), acting as a 'human animal' through whom the forces of an originary world pass.
signs.deamer_quote: “how the originary world captures up a body” (p. 88)
deleuze_examples: Greed (Erich von Stroheim, 1924) – McTeague and Trina consumed by the lust for gold (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Foolish Wives (Stroheim, 1922) – predatory impulses behind aristocratic manners (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
The Servant (Joseph Losey, 1963) – master and servant in a decaying house of impulses (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Viridiana (Luis Buñuel, 1961) – the beggars' orgy (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)

scenes: Two tourists walk through a dark forest in pouring rain toward a light, reaching the stark white modernist house of Dr Heiter.
Heiter in a tailored lab coat lectures his restrained subjects on operating tables with a slide presentation before the surgery.
The joined bodies crawl on hands and knees like an animal, stripped of speech.
The camera holds too long on Jenny gagging while Lindsey reaches out to take her hand.

signs.operation: Film a body taken over by appetite – eating, grabbing, crawling – so the act comes before any thought.
signs.shot_criteria: A figure (human or animal) visibly seized by raw drive: devouring food, fighting, clawing, crawling on all fours, frenzied grabbing at money or prey.
signs.gloss: characters overwhelmed by primal forces
signs.question: What force is acting through this body?

diff.name: Symptom
diff.difference: The body acts from a drive too strong for it: a visible primordial act (devouring, rutting, seizing, cruelty) in which the human behaves as a human animal, not as an agent with a goal.
diff.axis: where the primal force is lodged: in a body ([SYMPTOM — here]) → in an object (Fetish) → in the world-background (Originary world)

confusions.name: Fetish
confusions.flip: It is Fetish instead if the charge sits in an object the body has not yet seized — the scrap, shoe, relic held in insert — and no act has discharged it.
confusions.why_not: The Symptom is the discharge into a body; the Fetish is storage awaiting it.

confusions.name: Imprint
confusions.flip: It is Imprint instead if the violent act is the release of pressure slowly accumulated from a complex social situation, legible through a long build and an emotional object.
confusions.why_not: Deamer: the imprint's explosion 'is very different from the immediacy of the symptom'; the symptom is short-circuit, not accumulated behaviour.

confusions.name: Icon
confusions.flip: It is Icon instead if the face shows the intensity but the body stays still, the power not yet passing into an act.
confusions.why_not: A typical Symptom shot shows the act itself, often bodily, often not in close-up.

diff.counterfeit: A soldier firing in a battle scene is violent but not a Symptom — the act is situational, purposive action (action-image), not an impulse overwhelming the body.

confidence.high: A body visibly performing an appetitive or perverse act (eating raw, clawing, sexual compulsion, mindless cruelty) with animal-like posture and no strategic purpose.
confidence.medium: A violent or excessive act whose motive might be situational (revenge, self-defence) — could be Imprint or plain action.
confidence.low: A menacing or hungry-looking figure not yet acting; or any act whose drive-versus-goal status depends on narrative.

diff.deamer_anchor: "the impulse, which, by nature, is too strong for the character" (p. 88)

signs.name: Fetish
signs.definition: The secondary sign of the impulse-image: a partial or special object that stores the primal force of the originary world (charm, relic, scrap, shoe), holy or evil – relic or vult – awaiting the conditions to discharge it into a body.
signs.deamer_quote: “a special object charged with primal energies, awaiting a grounding” (p. 89)
deleuze_examples: Deleuze's list via Deamer (C1: 128): 'a haunch of meat, a raw morsel, a scrap, a woman's briefs, a shoe'
Diary of a Chambermaid (Luis Buñuel, 1964) – the old man's boot fetish (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Greed (Stroheim, 1924) – gold coins and the gilded canary cage (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)

section3.film: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows Parts 1 and 2 (David Yates, 2010–2011)
scenes: The horcruxes – Gaunt's ring, Riddle's diary, Hufflepuff's cup, Slytherin's locket, Ravenclaw's diadem – hunted and destroyed one by one.
'The Tale of the Three Brothers' in animated shadow-puppet style: Death hands over the elder wand, resurrection stone and cloak.
In the white King's Cross limbo, a foetus-like dying Voldemort curled beneath a bench – the horcrux torn from Harry.
After the final duel Harry snaps the elder wand in two.

signs.operation: Isolate one object in close-up and light it as if it holds a power, so the frame waits for someone to touch it.
signs.shot_criteria: An insert/close-up of a single charged object singled out and lit or held reverently: amulet, relic, idol, ring, locket, charm, shoe, key, a raw piece of meat.
signs.gloss: a special object charged with primal energies, awaiting a grounding
signs.question: What object has become charged?

diff.name: Fetish
diff.difference: A partial object is held apart and charged — relic or vult — so that the image makes us feel stored primal force in it, waiting for a body to discharge it.
diff.axis: where the primal force is lodged: in a body (Symptom) → in an object ([FETISH — here]) → in the world-background (Originary world)

confusions.name: Imprint
confusions.flip: It is Imprint instead if the object is an emotional token of a social situation (a murdered child's keepsake) linking a character's accumulated grievance to a milieu, rather than a vessel of pre-moral primal force.
confusions.why_not: The Fetish is prior to good and evil and outside history; the Imprint's object is a referent for a determined complex situation.

confusions.name: Mark
confusions.flip: It is Mark instead if the object's charge comes from habitual relation — it belongs to a familiar series (a cigarette case, a set of keys) and its meaning emerges when that series is recognised or broken.
confusions.why_not: A Mark or Demark is an object in a web of relations for the understanding; the Fetish's meaning is 'almost automatic', a drive-charge, not a logical relation.

confusions.name: Symptom
confusions.flip: It is Symptom instead if the object is already in the body's grip and the shot is about the act it compels (gnawing the meat, sniffing the shoe).
confusions.why_not: The Fetish shot typically isolates the object as potential, before or apart from the discharge.

diff.counterfeit: An insert close-up of a plot MacGuffin (a briefcase, a key) looks fetishistic but only carries information for the action; it has no primal charge.

confidence.high: A partial object isolated in close-up with ritual treatment (altar, glow, caressing hands, relic framing) and a sense of danger or sanctity beyond its use.
confidence.medium: A prominent object in insert whose charge could be either primal or plot-functional.
confidence.low: Any object shot without the body it will enter or the world it comes from; fetish status is conferred by the impulse circuit, which one shot rarely shows.

diff.deamer_anchor: "a retention awaiting a grounding" (p. 89)

signs.name: Originary world
signs.definition: The genetic sign of the impulse-image: a primal, archetypal background (desert, forest, swamp, the house) that rumbles beneath a determined milieu, outside history, under a curse of cyclical time tending toward entropy and ruin.
signs.deamer_quote: “the universe tending towards disintegration, collapse and entropy” (p. 90)
deleuze_examples: Greed (Stroheim, 1924) – Death Valley desert where the final struggle happens (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Ruby Gentry (King Vidor, 1952) – the swamp as primal world (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
The Exterminating Angel (Buñuel, 1962) – the salon sealed into a primal enclosure (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Deleuze's own terms (C1: 123): 'a house', 'desert', 'forest'

scenes: A walled park with lichen-covered waterfalls and a river where the schoolgirls swim, sealed off by high stone walls.
Static camera at the mouth of a night path: Bianca passes from pool to pool of electric lamplight strung in trees until the dark swallows her.
A newly arrived girl delivered unconscious in a coffin through tunnels beneath the woods and unlocked in the communal room.
A drowned runaway's coffin burned on a pyre at night as all the girls look on.

signs.operation: Frame the forest, desert or old house as something older than the story, and let it swallow the figures who cross it.
signs.shot_criteria: A primal environment dominating the frame with menace or timelessness – dense dark forest, desert, swamp, cave/tunnel, isolated old house, fire at night – with humans small or absent.
signs.gloss: a universe of primal forces
signs.question: What ancient or pre-social force underlies this milieu?

diff.name: Originary world
diff.difference: Beneath a recognisable place rumbles an archetypal one: the forest, desert, swamp or house is shown as a determinate but timeless ground of drives and decay, not as a historical setting.
diff.axis: where the primal force is lodged: in a body (Symptom) → in an object (Fetish) → in the world-background ([ORIGINARY WORLD — here])

confusions.name: Any-space-whatever
confusions.flip: It is Any-space-whatever instead if the space is indeterminate — a void, a fog, a colour field — expressing a pure affective quality with no specific primal place and no pressure on bodies.
confusions.why_not: The originary world only appears in the depths of a determined milieu; it is a specific archetypal place with forces, not pure indeterminacy.

confusions.name: Milieu
confusions.flip: It is Milieu instead if the place is historicised — dated architecture, social institutions, class markers laid out in establishing shots so actions exemplify a situation.
confusions.why_not: The originary world is outside or beneath history, cyclical time, entropy; it undoes the determined milieu rather than explaining behaviour.

confusions.name: Symptom
confusions.flip: It is Symptom instead if the shot's weight falls on a body already seized by the place's forces — the villager gone feral, the act of devouring — with the landscape reduced to backdrop.
confusions.why_not: The Originary world is the genetic ground itself: the forces are shown in the place (its decay, cyclical time) before or beyond any single body they capture.

diff.counterfeit: A picturesque forest in a hiking scene is just a location; without entropy, cruelty or primal pull on bodies it is Milieu, not the originary world.

confidence.high: An archetypal space (primeval forest, desert, the family house as lair) marked by decay, cyclicity or menace, with bodies in it visibly shrunk toward the animal.
confidence.medium: An archetypal place with atmosphere but no evidence of forces acting on bodies.
confidence.low: Any isolated landscape frame: resemblance to any-space-whatever is explicit in Deleuze, and determining 'beneath a milieu' needs the film.

diff.deamer_anchor: "not an any-space-whatever (although it may resemble one)" (p. 90)

signs.name: Index of lack
signs.definition: The first sign of the small-form action-image: the situation begins as an ellipsis, a hidden gap, which a character's actions progressively explore and then unequivocally reveal – and the reveal reorients what they do next.
signs.deamer_quote: “the situation is an ellipsis which is unequivocally revealed” (p. 93)
deleuze_examples: A Woman of Paris (Charlie Chaplin, 1923) – a train's arrival shown only by lights passing over the waiting woman's face (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)

The Immigrant (Chaplin, 1917) – Charlie seen from behind heaving over the rail as if seasick, then straightening with a fish on his line (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Deamer (C1: 160): the situation 'deduced from the action, by immediate inference'

scenes: Opening: a middle-aged woman in city clothes wanders a vast late-summer meadow and begins to dance alone – an image explained only at the end.
Do-joon absent-mindedly follows a schoolgirl down a dark street; she hides in a deserted building and throws a rock at him.
The mother searches for the truth, investigating the crime scene and witnesses herself.
Having learned her son is guilty, she presses an acupuncture point on her own thigh to erase the memory.

signs.operation: Withhold what is really happening and let a searcher's hands and eyes uncover it piece by piece until one image settles the question.
signs.shot_criteria: A shot of active searching or disclosure: someone investigating (with a flashlight, magnifier, opening a door, lifting a sheet, reading a clue) or an image whose meaning is revealed within the frame.
signs.gloss: the situation is an ellipsis which is unequivocally revealed
signs.question: What missing situation does this action let us infer?

diff.name: Index of lack
diff.difference: Something is visibly missing from the situation (an ellipsis) and the character's action fills it in one unequivocal disclosure that then redirects what they do.
diff.axis: situations an action reveals (small form, A→S): one, unequivocal ([INDEX OF LACK — here]) → two, undecidable (Index of equivocity) → many, a broken line across characters (Vector)

confusions.name: Index of equivocity
confusions.flip: It is Index of equivocity instead if the disclosure splits — the same act or clue points to two distant situations and the film refuses to settle which.
confusions.why_not: In the index of lack what is revealed is unequivocal; the reveal changes everything by determining the indeterminate.

confusions.name: Mark
confusions.flip: It is Mark/Demark instead if the revealing element is an object whose meaning comes from a habitual series being completed or broken — the thinking is done by the relation, not by the character's exploratory action.
confusions.why_not: Index of lack is an action-image: the situation is deduced from the character's action, not from a relational sign offered to the spectator's understanding.

confusions.name: Forking paths
confusions.flip: It is Forking paths instead if the gap is filled by competing flashback versions of the past rather than by present action.
confusions.why_not: The index of lack reveals a present situation through deeds; it does not branch the past.

diff.counterfeit: A cut that simply hides information and shows it later (a withheld shot) looks like an index of lack but is only editing ellipsis unless a character's action is the means of disclosure and the disclosure reorients their action.

confidence.high: Only across a sequence: an established gap, a character's investigating action, the unambiguous reveal, and a visible change in behaviour afterwards.
confidence.medium: A single 'discovery' shot (a character opens a door to the truth) when surrounding context is known.
confidence.low: Any isolated shot: this is an A→S→A′ structure; one shot can show at most one moment of it.

diff.deamer_anchor: "the situation is an ellipsis which is unequivocally revealed" (p. 93)

signs.name: Index of equivocity
signs.definition: The secondary sign of the small-form action-image: an action discloses a determined situation that nevertheless stays double – a slight difference relates one act to two distant situations, 'this and that', an impossible choice.
signs.deamer_quote: “The impossible choice. The world as fundamentally riven.” (p. 94)
deleuze_examples: Lubitsch comedies, e.g. Trouble in Paradise (Ernst Lubitsch, 1932) – a closed door or gesture implying two different situations (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
The Marriage Circle (Lubitsch, 1924) – misread gestures between two couples (cited by Deleuze in Cinema 1; Deamer's Section II names no films for this sign)
Deamer (C1: 161): 'made to hesitate by a whole world of details'

scenes: Deputy Lou Ford in a sunlit West Texas boom-town bedroom: the slap, the belt whipping, then the turn from rage to sex with Joyce.
Lou slowly pulling on black leather gloves while telling Joyce she will die; she laughs, thinking it is a game.
Two murders filmed utterly differently: Joyce beaten at length in cold, unflinching close shots; Elmer shot dead in an instant and the gun placed in Joyce's hand.
A web of motives surfaces (childhood abuse, a step-brother's death, jealousy) so no single reason explains the killings.

signs.operation: Stage one gesture so it points to two incompatible situations at once, and refuse to let the film choose between them.
signs.shot_criteria: A single visibly ambiguous action or composition that reads two ways: a gesture that could be tender or violent, a split/forked path, two doors, mirror or double framing, a smile over a threat.
signs.gloss: the situation is revealed as ambiguous
signs.question: What two worlds could explain the same action?

diff.name: Index of equivocity
diff.difference: An action discloses a situation that stays double: a slight difference in the same act refers it to two distant situations at once — 'this and that' — and the film sustains the undecidability.
diff.axis: situations an action reveals (small form, A→S): one, unequivocal (Index of lack) → two, undecidable ([INDEX OF EQUIVOCITY — here]) → many, a broken line across characters (Vector)

confusions.name: Index of lack
confusions.flip: It is Index of lack instead if a later action resolves which situation is true and the character reorients on that single reading.
confusions.why_not: The equivocal index is determined but riven; its ambiguity is a structure of the situation, not a delay before clarity.

confusions.name: Limpid and opaque
confusions.flip: It is Limpid and opaque (hyalosign) instead if the doubleness is between actual and virtual — a crystal image where the undecidable is whether we see the real or its reflection/memory — rather than between two actual situations.
confusions.why_not: The index of equivocity keeps both situations actual and within the sensory-motor schema; the hyalosign's indiscernibility is temporal/ontological.

confusions.name: Powers of the false
confusions.flip: It is Powers of the false instead if incompossible versions coexist and truth itself is suspended — the narrator/character is a forger and no situation is determinable at all.
confusions.why_not: Deamer insists the equivocal situation is 'no less determined'; the two poles are both true readings of one world.

diff.counterfeit: A red-herring shot in a mystery (a suspicious glance that is later explained away) looks equivocal but is an Index of lack with a delay.

confidence.high: Only across the film: a character's act visibly readable as two incompatible situations, still unresolved at the end or resolved as both.
confidence.medium: A single act staged with an explicit double reading (e.g. a gesture tender and menacing at once) when the film's structure is known.
confidence.low: Any isolated shot; ambiguity in one shot is cheap and may be mere uncertainty.

diff.deamer_anchor: "a slight difference ... to relate it to two quite distant situations" (p. 93)

signs.name: Vector
signs.definition: The genetic sign of the small form: many characters each reveal a partial situation, and together these ellipses form a broken, unpredictable but necessary line that maps one heterogeneous yet homogeneous world.
signs.deamer_quote: "a very powerful image of the heterogeneity composing a homogeneous world" (p. 95)
deleuze_examples: Man of the West (Anthony Mann, 1958) — the neo-western 'skeleton-space' with missing intermediaries
The Wild Bunch (Sam Peckinpah, 1969) — the 'incongruous makeshift group' with a debt to discharge
NOTE: Deamer's Section II gives no film examples; these are Deleuze's own Cinema 1 examples (not cited by Deamer); attribution from memory of C1: 165-168, verify

scenes: Five interlocking episodes (Omar, Malek, Dando, Binj, Abu Elias) set in one Yafa district: the lead of one story walks through the background of another, so a single street holds several separate situations.
Malek, an undocumented worker, labours in a restaurant kitchen for his dying mother while the restaurateur's family plot runs on around him: two situations in one workplace.
Dando, a Jewish cop, searches the streets for his missing brother, crossing the Arab characters' lines without resolving them: ellipses carried from one episode into another.
The district itself (Muslims, Jews, Christians, Bedouin, three kinds of law) shown as a patchwork of locations rather than one encompassing milieu: 'Israels', not Israel.

signs.operation: Cut between several characters on separate missions through one place, and let each thread leave a gap that another thread fills.
signs.shot_criteria: One frame holds several independent people, vehicles or creatures in one shared space, each clearly moving along its own path or doing its own task, with no single centre.
signs.gloss: multiple situations within the homogeneous universe
signs.question: How do several incomplete situations compose a world?

diff.name: Vector
diff.difference: Many characters each disclose a partial, equivocal situation, and only their interlocking over the film draws the broken, unpredictable but necessary line of one world.
diff.axis: situations an action reveals (small form, A→S): one, unequivocal (Index of lack) → two, undecidable (Index of equivocity) → many, a broken line across characters ([VECTOR — here])

confusions.name: Index of equivocity
confusions.flip: It is Index of equivocity instead if the film has one principal character facing a two-sided situation rather than a multiplicity of disclosers.
confusions.why_not: The Vector is a nexus of indices distributed across an ensemble; its world is heterogeneous yet homogeneous.

confusions.name: Liquid perception
confusions.flip: It is Liquid perception instead if the ensemble is only a flow of perceived centres with no situation being disclosed by their actions.
confusions.why_not: Liquid perception organises what is seen; the Vector organises what the actions reveal about a shared world.

confusions.name: Forking paths
confusions.flip: It is Forking paths instead if the multiple lines are alternative versions of the past told through recollection rather than simultaneous present situations.
confusions.why_not: The vector's situations are 'a priori simultaneous', determined in one world; forking paths branch memory.

diff.counterfeit: A hyperlink ensemble film whose storylines merely coincide (a car crash links strangers) looks like a vector, but if the strands disclose no common situation it is closer to Liquid perception.

confidence.high: Only at film scale: an ensemble whose separate strands, each partially revealing, converge on the lines of force of one heterogeneous world (city of tribes).
confidence.medium: A sequence cross-cutting several characters' disclosures when the film's overall structure is known.
confidence.low: Any single shot; the vector is by definition a relation among many situations and cannot be present in one image.

diff.deamer_anchor: "a broken line whose path is unpredictable, although necessary" (p. 94)

signs.name: Milieu
signs.definition: The first sign of the large form: a fully determined geographical, historical and social situation (the Encompasser), laid out through establishing and extreme wide shots, whose characters' actions merely exemplify it.
signs.deamer_quote: "The characters are one with the milieu and the milieu at one with the characters." (p. 99)
deleuze_examples: Nanook of the North (Robert Flaherty, 1922) — the ice field as encompassing milieu
The Grapes of Wrath (John Ford, 1940) — the Dust Bowl situation that determines the family's migration
NOTE: Deamer's Section II gives no film examples; these are Deleuze's own Cinema 1 examples (not cited by Deamer); verify against C1 ch. 9

section3.film: marxism today (prologue) (Phil Collins, 2010), with its untitled sequel
scenes: Archive footage of an East German classroom: a lecturer chalks a pyramid (director at apex, workers at the base) and writes 'exploitation' on the blackboard.
The lecturer turns 'exploitation' into 'exploitation?' after a student says his West German uncle owns a car and washing machine: a whole social system diagrammed in one frame.
Talking-head monologues of three former Marxist-Leninist lecturers recount life before and after reunification, the milieu traced along a time axis (S → S`).
The sequel: a present-day lecture on Capital in modern Germany, product versus commodity, echoing the archive classroom shot for shot.

signs.operation: Open wide on the whole social and geographic world, and only then let people move inside it as expressions of that world.
signs.shot_criteria: An establishing or extreme wide shot where the environment (town, landscape, factory, institution, classroom system) dominates and the people are small parts of it; or an explanatory diagram of a social order.
signs.gloss: the situation explicated through character actions
signs.question: What world produces these actions?

diff.name: Milieu
diff.difference: The situation is given before anyone acts: an establishing or extreme wide shot lays out a determined geo-historical and social space, and the people in it exemplify it rather than change it.
diff.axis: how the given situation bears on action (large form, S→A): spread out and exemplified ([MILIEU — here]) → split into two duelling forces (Binomial) → internalised in one body until it explodes (Imprint)

confusions.name: Binomial
confusions.flip: It is Binomial instead if the frame is organised by two opposed forces squaring off (two camps, two lines, a standoff) so the setting is only the stage of a duel.
confusions.why_not: In the Milieu the situation is foreground and action derivative (SAS, things remain as they are).

confusions.name: Originary world
confusions.flip: It is Originary world instead if the place is timeless and primal — an archetypal forest or house rumbling with drives and entropy — rather than historically and socially dated.
confusions.why_not: The Milieu is historicised realism; the originary world lies beneath history.

confusions.name: Quotidian
confusions.flip: It is Quotidian instead if the everyday life shown is a reflection-image that turns the large form around — ordinary, un-heroic banality that deflates or inverts the action form.
confusions.why_not: The Milieu presents everyday existence as determined situation feeding action, without inversion or critique of the form.

diff.counterfeit: An aerial drone shot of a city used as a scenic transition looks like an establishing Milieu shot but, if nothing in the film is derived from that situation, it is just location, or even Gaseous perception if manipulated.

confidence.high: An extreme wide/establishing shot rich in specific historical, geographic and social markers (period architecture, institutions, labour) with small figures embedded in it as its exemplars.
confidence.medium: A wide shot of a place with some specificity but no evidence that behaviour is derived from it.
confidence.low: A generic wide shot; whether actions 'exemplify' the milieu is a film-level relation.

diff.deamer_anchor: "a predominance of establishing shots and extreme wide shots" (p. 99)

signs.name: Binomial
signs.definition: The second sign of the large form: the milieu splits into two opposed lines of force embodied by characters, and the film proceeds through duels (violent, romantic, political) converging on a final decisive one.
signs.deamer_quote: "The film is pure action from beginning to end." (p. 100)
deleuze_examples: The Birth of a Nation (D. W. Griffith, 1915) — parallel then convergent montage towards the final duel/rescue
NOTE: Deamer's Section II gives no film examples; these are Deleuze's own Cinema 1 examples (not cited by Deamer); verify against C1 ch. 9

scenes: Sandra, in a yellow dressing gown, crosses the vast empty Ford shop floor to a photoshoot corner and drapes herself over a car.
Close-up: EQUAL PAY written in red lipstick across her belly, turning a cheesecake pose into a declaration of the strike.
Cut up to the glass-fronted office above the floor: the American boss flown in to break the strike turns and walks away, the duel won in a look.
Rita O'Grady leads the women sewing machinists against management, union, husbands and government: a whole film of duels on one gendered line of force.

signs.operation: Split the world into two sides, give each a face, and cut back and forth between them until they meet in a confrontation.
signs.shot_criteria: Two opposed parties (people, groups, animals) visibly face or confront each other in the frame, or one side stares down the other across a clear divide.
signs.gloss: a whole world of duels
signs.question: Where has the world become a duel?

diff.name: Binomial
diff.difference: Two opposed lines of force, embodied in characters, face each other: the image is organised as a duel (violent, romantic, political) pointing toward a decisive confrontation.
diff.axis: how the given situation bears on action (large form, S→A): spread out and exemplified (Milieu) → split into two duelling forces ([BINOMIAL — here]) → internalised in one body until it explodes (Imprint)

confusions.name: Milieu
confusions.flip: It is Milieu instead if the figures are present only as instances of their world, with no opposition structuring the frame.
confusions.why_not: In the Binomial the milieu is merely the staging ground; action is foreground, 'pure action from beginning to end'.

confusions.name: Index of equivocity
confusions.flip: It is Index of equivocity instead if the two sides are two readings of one situation revealed by an act, rather than two opposed forces meeting in combat.
confusions.why_not: Binomial duality is conflict between forces (S→A); equivocal duality is ambiguity of disclosure (A→S).

confusions.name: Mirrors face to face
confusions.flip: It is Mirrors face to face instead if the two facing figures are doubles whose images multiply into each other, confusing actual and virtual, rather than adversaries resolving a situation.
confusions.why_not: The Binomial's two poles are distinct and the duel produces a victory and a new situation (SAS′).

diff.counterfeit: A shot/reverse-shot conversation between two people framed symmetrically looks duel-like, but without opposed lines of force and a trajectory to a decisive clash it is ordinary dialogue coverage.

confidence.high: A standoff or confrontation framing two embodied opposing sides (two strikers vs management, two gunfighters), recognised as one duel in a proliferation leading to a final one.
confidence.medium: A single confrontation shot with clear opposition, but unknown whether duels structure the film.
confidence.low: Two people in frame without evident opposition; or any shot where the 'polynomial' duel structure must be inferred.

diff.deamer_anchor: "two dominant lines of force ... embodied in the characters" (p. 100)

signs.name: Imprint
signs.definition: The genetic sign of the large form: a complex milieu is internalised by a character, accumulating as pressure until it explodes into action, and made visible through an emotional object that links the character to the situation.
signs.deamer_quote: "an indelible impression of the world upon a character" (p. 101)
deleuze_examples: On the Waterfront (Elia Kazan, 1954) — Kazan's behaviourism of internal factors
East of Eden (Elia Kazan, 1955)
Godzilla (Ishiro Honda, 1954) — subject of Deamer's own essay 'An imprint of Godzilla' (cited in front matter)
NOTE: Deamer's Section II gives no film examples; these are Deleuze's own Cinema 1 examples (not cited by Deamer) (Kazan per C1: 157-159, verify)

scenes: Mia dances alone in an abandoned flat with ripped wallpaper and tatty carpet, trying to exhaust the rage the estate has loaded into her.
Near some caravans Mia finds a thin, chained-up horse and keeps trying to free it; its death later releases her tears: the emotional object.
Left behind by Connor, the 'California Dreaming' CD spins on at the audition as Mia walks off the stage.
On the estate Mia interrupts girls dancing for the lads and their dogs and it ends in a head-butt: one of the local duels that fill her up.

signs.operation: Load the character with the world scene by scene, give that pressure one object to hold, and let the release come late and violently.
signs.shot_criteria: A lone figure visibly weighed down by their surroundings, or a charged personal object (toy, record, photo, animal) shown in close relation to a person, so the environment reads as pressing on them.
signs.gloss: an indelible impression of the world upon a character
signs.question: How has the world gotten inside the character?

diff.name: Imprint
diff.difference: A complex situation has entered one body: the character carries it as visible, contained pressure, often fixed on an emotional object that links them to the world, before (or as) it bursts into action.
diff.axis: how the given situation bears on action (large form, S→A): spread out and exemplified (Milieu) → split into two duelling forces (Binomial) → internalised in one body until it explodes ([IMPRINT — here])

confusions.name: Symptom
confusions.flip: It is Symptom instead if the outburst is immediate and appetitive, a primal drive with no accumulated social situation behind it.
confusions.why_not: Deamer: the imprint's release accumulates over the sequence and 'is very different from the immediacy of the symptom'.

confusions.name: Icon
confusions.flip: It is Icon instead if the charged face expresses a quality or power purely in itself, not as the internalisation of a determined milieu.
confusions.why_not: The Imprint is an action-image: the internal state is legibly the milieu pressed into a body and destined for action.

confusions.name: Binomial
confusions.flip: It is Binomial instead if the pressure is externalised as a face-off between two embodied camps, the conflict played out between characters rather than stored inside one.
confusions.why_not: In the Imprint the polynomial duels are internalised in a single body; the gap between milieu and act (fifth law) is bridged slowly inside the character, and the outcome tends to deterioration (SAS″).

diff.counterfeit: A brooding close-up of an angry teenager looks like an imprint, but if no milieu has been shown pressing in and no action follows it is only an Icon.

confidence.high: Across a sequence: a character repeatedly shown absorbing a cramped, complex milieu, an emotional object recurrent, then the explosive act.
confidence.medium: A single shot of a character clutching or staring at a charged object amid a legible hostile environment.
confidence.low: Any isolated face or outburst; the internalisation and delayed release are temporal and relational.

diff.deamer_anchor: "the inner, but visible, link ... and the explosive action" (p. 101)

signs.name: Plastic figure
signs.definition: Deamer's first sign of composition of the attraction-image: a small-form film is transformed by the large form, so an on-screen action, object or episode works as metaphor, metonymy or synecdoche for an implied situation that stays in ellipsis.
signs.deamer_quote: "an object which has a meaning beyond itself" (p. 107)
deleuze_examples: Strike (Sergei Eisenstein, 1925) — the massacre of workers intercut with a slaughtered bull

NOTE: Deamer's Section II gives no film examples; these are Deleuze's own Cinema 1 examples (not cited by Deamer); attribution from memory of C1 ch. 11, verify. Also note Deamer's table Fig. I.18 lists Theatrical first and Plastic second, the reverse of his Section II text

scenes: In drought-stricken Kaohsiung, Shiang-chyi sees hundreds of watermelons floating in the sluggish Love River: the fruit replaces water.
Alone, she pushes a watermelon under her top and mimes pregnancy and birth.
Shiang-chyi finds her lost suitcase key set into the tarmac, but even when retrieved it will not open the case.
Garish musical numbers break in: a merman in a water tank, dancers with umbrellas in a dragon waterpark, costumes in watermelon green, red and black.

signs.operation: Let one object or eruption stand in for the situation you refuse to show directly.
signs.shot_criteria: A single object, creature or staged spectacle clearly standing in for something larger (metaphor/metonymy), for example fruit in place of water, animal slaughter in place of massacre, or a sudden stylised musical number.
signs.gloss: small form transformed by the large form, an implied situation
signs.question: What greater situation does this action unexpectedly imply?

diff.difference: Does a single on-screen object, action or cut stand in, in one stroke, for a real situation that is never itself shown (metaphor/metonymy/synecdoche), while the film's own drive is still action discovering situation?
diff.axis: trope that converts one action-form into the other: [perfect trope in one moment, small form carried by large (eS(S))] → imperfect trope sustained over a sequence, large form carried by small (S→iA) → nesting so recursive you cannot tell which form contains which

confusions.name: Theatrical figure
confusions.flip: It is Theatrical instead if the figure is not a single substituted image but a staged fictitious action (a play, game, rehearsal, parody) that runs over a sequence and prefigures a real act the film keeps deferring.
confusions.why_not: A plastic figure is instantaneous and substitutive: the slaughtered bull replaces the massacre in one cut; nothing is rehearsed or deferred.

confusions.name: Symbol
confusions.flip: It is a Symbol instead if the object's meaning is an abstract relation that organises the whole plot (a key, a necklace binding characters in a Hitchcockian relation) rather than a figure for a situation kept in ellipsis.
confusions.why_not: The plastic figure points past itself to a real situation the film does not show; the symbol is a concrete object carrying a relation the film does show being exchanged.

confusions.name: Index of lack
confusions.flip: It is an Index of lack instead if the shown action is literal and simply lets us infer an unshown situation (an elision in the chain of events), with no figural substitution.
confusions.why_not: The index of lack is inference from a gap; the plastic figure is a trope: the shown thing means something other than itself.

diff.counterfeit: An insert of a ticking clock during a wait looks like a plastic figure but is only a literal action-image detail (time pressure inside the situation), not a trope standing for an unshown situation.

confidence.high: A cut or insert substitutes an unrelated image for an event the film never shows directly, and the substitution is legible as metaphor/metonymy (Strike's bull for the workers).
confidence.medium: A recurring object that the film loads with meaning beyond its narrative use, but the implied situation is partly shown too.
confidence.low: Any 'meaningful' object whose significance is only interpretive and not built by editing or repetition.

diff.deamer_anchor: "an object which has a meaning beyond itself" (p. 107)

signs.name: Theatrical figure
signs.definition: Deamer's second sign of composition of the attraction-image: a large-form film is transformed by the small form, so the real situation is expressed through a sustained fictitious action (allegory, myth, parody) that prefigures and keeps deferring the real action.
signs.deamer_quote: "a sequence of images as precursor of the real action" (p. 107)
deleuze_examples: To Be or Not to Be (Ernst Lubitsch, 1942) — theatrical performance prefiguring real action
NOTE: Deamer's Section II gives no film examples; these are Deleuze's own Cinema 1 examples (not cited by Deamer); attribution uncertain, verify against C1: 182-183

section3.film: Scott Pilgrim vs. the World (Edgar Wright, 2010)
scenes: In a vast warehouse club Scott, flaming samurai sword in hand, cuts through Gideon's henchmen, who burst into showers of coins as points float up.
Horizontal split-screen of the two rivals' faces, then a slow-motion mid-air sword clash haloed in white light, with sound rendered as graphics.
Each evil ex is fought as a video-game level; beaten bodies dissolve into coins and Scott earns extra lives.
Comic-book effects: a punch launches a man into the sky, a giant mallet appears from nowhere, a sword emerges from Scott's chest.

signs.operation: Stage the real conflict as a game, play or mock battle, and repeat it until it stands in for the fight itself.
signs.shot_criteria: A visibly staged, rehearsed, cartoon or mock version of a conflict (drill, puppet fight, stage duel, war game, animated battle) standing in for a real one.
signs.gloss: a sequence of images as precursor of the real action
signs.question: What real action is being rehearsed through fiction?

diff.difference: Is a fictitious action (performance, game, allegory, parody) being played out over a sequence as a precursor of a real action that has not yet happened and keeps being deferred?
diff.axis: trope that converts one action-form into the other: perfect trope in one moment, small form carried by large (eS(S)) → [imperfect trope sustained over a sequence, large form carried by small (S→iA)] → nesting so recursive you cannot tell which form contains which

confusions.name: Plastic figure
confusions.flip: It is Plastic instead if the figure collapses into one substituted image or cut rather than a sustained performed sequence.
confusions.why_not: The theatrical figure is linear and repeated; it needs duration and at least one repetition to prefigure.

confusions.name: Mise en abyme
confusions.flip: It is Mise en abyme instead if the performance contains figures that in turn contain the performance, so we cannot tell which level is the real action and which the rehearsal.
confusions.why_not: In a theatrical figure the real/fictitious hierarchy holds: the play prefigures, the real act eventually arrives (or is known to be the thing deferred).

confusions.name: Powers of the false
confusions.flip: It is Powers of the false instead if there is no real action the performance prefigures at all: every level is equally a forgery and truth is no longer the horizon.
confusions.why_not: The theatrical figure is still a movement-image trope: it depends on a real action to come.

diff.counterfeit: A scene of actors on a stage in a backstage musical looks theatrical, but if the show is just the narrative's own situation (putting on a show) it is plain action-image, not a figure prefiguring some other real action.

confidence.high: A staged fiction is repeated and its structure visibly maps onto a real confrontation that follows (To Be or Not to Be's performance becoming the escape).
confidence.medium: An allegorical sequence whose correspondence to the real action is clear but unrepeated.
confidence.low: A single shot of a performance: whether it prefigures anything cannot be seen in the shot.

diff.deamer_anchor: "a sequence of images as precursor of the real action" (p. 107)

signs.name: Mise en abyme
signs.definition: Deamer's own name for the genetic sign Deleuze leaves unnamed: plastic and theatrical figures nest inside each other so we cannot tell which form contains which, an image within an image within an image.
signs.deamer_quote: "It is as if we enter and become lost in a hall of mirrors" (p. 108)
deleuze_examples: None: Deleuze neither names nor describes this sign (Deamer, p. 108)

scenes: Time freezes on the commuter train: the camera tracks back down the carriage past passengers stuck mid-laugh, a comedian mid-punchline and spilt coffee hanging in the air.
Colter Stevens wakes, again and again, in a replica helicopter cockpit, a plastic figure of the place he died that holds together and decays with his consciousness.
The same eight minutes on the train, re-entered repeatedly with variations: a theatrical figure that becomes a new real.
His real body, a bagged and tagged mutilated trunk on life support, is revealed as the ground beneath both figures.

signs.operation: Nest the scene inside a replica of itself (screen, model, mirror, loop) until the frame and the framed trade places.
signs.shot_criteria: An image visibly contains another image or replica of itself or its world: a screen showing a screen, mirrors facing each other, a model within the scene, a film being shown inside the film.
signs.gloss: a recurrence of plastic and theatrical figures
signs.question: Is one action-world nested inside another?

diff.difference: Do figures nest inside figures such that, watching, you cannot say whether a performed sequence contains an emblematic image or an emblematic image contains the performed sequence?
diff.axis: trope that converts one action-form into the other: perfect trope in one moment, small form carried by large (eS(S)) → imperfect trope sustained over a sequence, large form carried by small (S→iA) → [nesting so recursive you cannot tell which form contains which]

confusions.name: Theatrical figure
confusions.flip: It is Theatrical instead if the nested performance has a clear outside: one real action that the play-within points toward.
confusions.why_not: Mise en abyme loses the outside; the recursion is the point.

confusions.name: Mirrors face to face
confusions.flip: It is Mirrors face to face instead if the recursion is optical, actual and virtual images exchanging in literal reflective surfaces with no trope or narrative prefiguring at stake.
confusions.why_not: Mise en abyme is a recursion of figures (tropes of action and situation); the crystal is a recursion of the actual/virtual image itself, time-image not action.

confusions.name: Powers of the false
confusions.flip: It is Powers of the false instead if the nested levels are incompossible versions with no true one and the characters are forgers of time.
confusions.why_not: Mise en abyme still converts action-forms; it disorients reflection but does not abolish the true.

diff.counterfeit: A shot of a TV playing the same film we are watching looks like mise en abyme, but if it is a one-off gag that does not fold the film's small and large forms into one another it is only a visual quip.

confidence.high: A film where the frame-within repeatedly becomes the frame (Source Code's loop in a replica cockpit) and the viewer loses which level is originary.
confidence.medium: A strong image-within-image that recurs but whose top level stays secure.
confidence.low: A single frame-within-frame composition; visual nesting alone is not the sign.

signs.name: Figure of the sublime
signs.definition: The first sign of composition of the inversion-image (SAS becomes sAs): a visionary character dreams up an action far larger than the situation requires, so the over-reaction exposes the situation, and the plan, as futile.
signs.deamer_quote: "a film in which the behaviours of the character overwhelm the givens of the situation" (p. 111)
deleuze_examples: Aguirre, the Wrath of God (Werner Herzog, 1972) — the conquistador's mad river expedition
Fitzcarraldo (Werner Herzog, 1982) — hauling a steamship over a mountain
NOTE: Deamer's Section II gives no film examples; these are Deleuze's own Cinema 1 examples (not cited by Deamer) (C1: 184-185)

scenes: Grainy 4:3 video, front-on at eye level: Waj sits cross-legged before a faded wall-hanging holding a Kalashnikov (actually a toy; he says he has 'big hands') for his martyrdom video.
A cell member dies in an accident with homemade explosives, a dry-stone wall and a flock of sheep.
Waj and Hassan shake their heads continuously to blur the CCTV cameras.
At the training camp Omar fires the rocket launcher backwards and blows up the camp during a drone strike.

signs.operation: Give a small person an absurdly grand plan and film the plan's execution with total solemnity.
signs.shot_criteria: A visible act of grandiose over-reach or zealous spectacle, oversized relative to its means or setting: a lone zealot, a doomed grand machine, a mass rally, a stunt that fails.
signs.gloss: actions surpass the determinates of an enfeebled situation
signs.question: Is the action bigger than the world requires?

diff.difference: Does the character's action visibly exceed anything the situation requires, so that the grandiose act makes the situation look futile (a steamship hauled over a mountain)?
diff.axis: where the disproportion between action and situation lies: [action outsizes a futile situation (sAs)] → futile action reveals an immense situation (aSa) → sAs = aSa, trivial and immense indistinguishable

confusions.name: Figure of enfeeblement
confusions.flip: It is Enfeeblement instead if the character is small, aimless and ineffective and it is the world that swells up around them.
confusions.why_not: In the sublime the character is the outsized force; the world shrinks to a futile encompasser.

confusions.name: Milieu
confusions.flip: It is Milieu instead if the situation determines and justifies the heroic response, a large-form SAS where action answers the milieu and modifies it.
confusions.why_not: The sublime action is not required by the situation; the ratio between act and givens is broken.

confusions.name: Imprint
confusions.flip: It is an Imprint instead if the excess is interior and explained: a psychological obsession or buried drive drives the act and the film reads it as character causality.
confusions.why_not: The sublime is hallucinatory and visionary; the act exposes the situation as absurd rather than exposing the character's hidden motive.

diff.counterfeit: An action hero single-handedly storming a fortress looks sublime, but if the plot's threat really does require the feat it is large-form action (SAS), not an inverted sAs.

confidence.high: The enterprise is visibly absurd relative to its goal and the film stages it as hypnotic or visionary (Aguirre, Fitzcarraldo, Four Lions' plan).
confidence.medium: Over-reaction is clear but the film partly endorses it as justified.
confidence.low: A single spectacular gesture without knowledge of what the situation demanded.

diff.deamer_anchor: "the behaviours of the character overwhelm the givens of the situation" (p. 111)
